slides.notes:
Hi, we are Team Cosmic Cats from Amman. Our project is Analog Atlas.
In one sentence: it finds the Moon and Mars on Earth, using real, sourced data, not guesses. Values are measured where possible; where they are not, the app says 'not measured'.

items.text: NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE 2026 · AMMAN
ANALOG ATLAS
Find the Moon and Mars on Earth.
A 3D atlas of the places on Earth that behave like the Moon and Mars, built on real, sourced data.
Challenge: Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars
Team Cosmic Cats

Mohammad Fathi Awni Ahmad · Ameer Hamam
Abdalrhman Ali Samih Alhaj Hassan · Moath Abu Aisha
App screenshot · Earth: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble (NASA GIBS)

slides.notes:
To go to the Moon or Mars, NASA first tests everything on Earth, in places called analogs.
Look at these two photos: one is the Moon, one is Iceland. Hard to tell!
But looking alike is not enough. Which places really match a Moon base site or a Mars landing zone, in temperature, ground and rock? The data exists, but it is spread over many datasets.

items.text: 01 · THE PROBLEM
Before anyone flies, everything is tested on Earth.

Crews, rovers, suits and drills train in “analog” places on Earth.
But which places really behave like a Moon base site or a Mars landing zone?
The answer is spread over many NASA datasets, and analogs are often picked by how they look.
One is the Moon. One is Iceland.
THE MOON · Apollo 11, 1969
EARTH · Holuhraun, Iceland
Photos: NASA / Neil Armstrong, Apollo 11 (panorama assembly Yuri Krasilnikov) · NASA Johnson Space Center / Robert Markowitz. Public domain.

slides.notes:
Analog Atlas is a 3D globe of Earth, the Moon and Mars that runs in the browser.
You pick one of 13 targets, for example Jezero Crater on Mars or one of three permanent Moon base sites near the south pole, and the app ranks 19 Earth sites by how closely they match it.
You can fly to each place, stand there, and compare real photos side by side in Twin view.

items.text: 02 · OUR SOLUTION
Analog Atlas
A 3D globe of Earth, the Moon and Mars, in the browser.

Pick one of 13 targets: 3 Moon base sites, Moon ice, a Moon cave, Apollo sites, Mars landing sites and a Mars cave.
It ranks 19 Earth analog sites on 6 continents, with open, sourced data.
Fly down to any place in 3D and stand there.
Twin view: real photos of the Earth site and its target, side by side.
Twin view · Harrat al-Shaam (Jordan) and Jezero Crater (Mars)
The Moon’s south pole · Malapert Massif
App screenshots. Photos: Mohammad hajeer / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (cropped) · NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/ASU · Moon: NASA LRO

slides.notes:
Each Earth site gets a score from five pillars: climate, terrain, landing zone, geology and resources.
For the Moon base sites, climate also compares Sun height, how high the Sun gets in the sky, computed from latitude on both sides.
Climate, terrain and landing zone come from data: NASA POWER and MODIS on Earth, LRO on the Moon, NASA's orbiters and rovers on Mars, and elevation maps of all three worlds. Rock type and resources are sourced classifications: each one has a published source and an exact quote.
Where a value is a general figure and not a measurement at the site, the app labels it, and weak data gets a flag. If something was not measured, the app says 'not measured'. We never invent a number.
Satellites also show what the ground is made of: MODIS, Sentinel-2, ASTER and NASA's EMIT. The app shows it next to the score, but it never changes the score.

items.text: 03 · HOW WE SCORE
Five pillars, every value with its source.

items.title: Climate
items.body: Mean temperature, daily swing, coldest ground, rain and albedo. Moon base sites add Sun height.
items.source: NASA POWER 2001–2020 · MODIS · LRO Diviner · Mars Climate Sounder

items.title: Terrain
items.body: How steep the ground is in a 10 km box, on the same 500 m grid on all three worlds.
items.source: Copernicus DEM · LRO LOLA · MGS MOLA

items.title: Landing zone
items.body: The largest flat square where every slope is under 10°, after NASA’s Artemis landing rule (our slopes are over 1 km, NASA’s over 100 m).

items.title: Geology
items.body: The main rock type: the same, related or different.

items.title: Resources
items.body: Water ice, caves for shelter, regolith to build with, salts and brines.
items.source: Every tag has a source and an exact quote

items.text: No guessing: a value that was not measured is shown as “not measured”, and weak data gets a ⚑ flag.
Also measured from orbit, shown but never scored: MODIS, Sentinel-2, ASTER and NASA EMIT show what the top of the ground is made of.
Photo: Harrat al-Shaam, Mohammad hajeer / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (cropped, darkened)

slides.notes:
Here are some results.
For Jezero Crater, where Perseverance is driving, the best Earth twin is Harrat al-Shaam, the black basalt desert in north-east Jordan, at 71 percent. It also has lava caves, and it comes first for the cave targets on the Moon and Mars.
Harrat al-Shaam also comes first for the Apollo 11 and Apollo 17 sites, at 69 and 64 percent. We apply one rule to every regolith tag, and the simulant source for SP Crater in Arizona names a cone about 40 kilometres away, so SP Crater lost that tag. Apollo 11 carries a flag in the app: most of its values are Moon-wide figures, not measurements at the site.
For the permanent Moon base sites near the south pole, Antarctica's Dry Valleys come first for Malapert, at 62 percent, Rio Tinto in Spain for Mons Mouton, and Jordan's Wadi Rum shares first place with Rio Tinto for the Shackleton connecting ridge, at 56 percent. These three use only 3 of 5 pillars. Their climate now includes Sun height, how high the Sun gets, the same formula on Earth and Moon, so polar Earth sites match best on climate. But the order still comes mostly from slope and the flat landing zone. Taken together, Haughton Crater in Canada is the only Earth site in the top 5 for all three base sites.
A score is not proof. It tells you where to test first.
Then we scored all of Jordan, 886 boxes of 10 kilometres, with the same method. For most targets the best boxes are on the same Harrat basalt plain as our hand-picked site, or close to one of our sites, and score within two points of the best hand-picked Jordan site. So for 9 of the 13 targets the data confirms our picks, and shows that the Harrat basalt is a whole plain, not one point. For two Moon base sites, Mons Mouton and the Shackleton ridge, single mountain boxes lead, on slope only. For the Shackleton crater floor, granite boxes next to Wadi Rum lead, only because granite is in the same rock family as anorthosite. For Phoenix, our Lisan Peninsula site stays ahead. The basalt stands out mainly because its rock type matches. Nobody has checked these boxes on the ground yet.

items.text: 04 · WHAT WE FOUND
Earth twins of the Moon and Mars

Full analog match, default weights; a match says where to test first, not proof. Moon base sites use 3 of 5 pillars. Haughton is the only Earth site in the top 5 for all 3 base sites; each site alone has a different #1, mostly on slope (Malapert: McMurdo Dry Valleys 62 %). Data flag ⚑: the climate cells of Tso Kar and the Dry Valleys sit over 400 m off the ground.
Discover Jordan

We scored all of Jordan the same way: 886 boxes of 10 km. For 9 of 13 targets the best boxes are on or near our chosen sites: the data confirms them. For 2 Moon base sites, mountain boxes lead on slope.
Discover Jordan: each square is a 10 km box, not field-checked
App screenshot. Climate: NASA POWER · terrain: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 · geology: IGME5000, © BGR, Hannover, 2005 (modified) · boundary: Natural Earth · Earth: Bing Maps Aerial via Cesium ion

slides.notes:
We also built a small field kit: an ESP32 with six sensors, including UV. It plugs into the app by USB, logs a full day, and compares that day with NASA's numbers.
Our honest status: so far the kit data is simulated. Our next step is a real 24-hour log at a Jordan site.
After that: a geologist's review of our rock map, more countries, and sharing the atlas with people who plan analog missions, and with students.

items.text: 05 · FROM DATA TO THE FIELD
Our field kit checks the ground itself.

An ESP32 with six sensors: air temperature and humidity, soil temperature, infrared surface temperature, UV, and sunlight up and down for albedo.
It plugs into the app by USB, logs 24 hours, and compares the day with NASA data.
Next steps

Record a real 24-hour log at a Jordan site (so far, all kit data is simulated).
Have a geologist review our rock map of Jordan.
Bring Discover to more countries.
Share the atlas with analog mission teams, students and teachers.
Photo: Wadi Rum, Hansueli Krapf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 (cropped, darkened, drawing added)
